# OpenGlass UI: full consumer reference

OpenGlass UI (`open-glass-ui` on npm, MIT, zero runtime dependencies) is a React
UI system built from glass materials: forty accessible native-DOM recipes,
neutral adaptive themes, CSS-first glass, explicit SVG/SDF refraction and an
opt-in WebGL2 surface for media you own.

This file ships inside the npm package, so it describes the version you have
installed. Read it from `node_modules/open-glass-ui/llms-full.txt`. Check the
installed version in `node_modules/open-glass-ui/package.json` before relying on
anything newer than it. Repository: https://github.com/moekoelueker/open-glass-ui.
Live demo: https://moelueker.com/liquid-glass.

OpenGlass UI is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or
sponsored by Apple Inc. It does not promise pixel parity with a proprietary
native renderer and must not use Apple assets, fonts or branding.

## 1. Install, stylesheet and provider

```sh
npm install open-glass-ui react react-dom
```

React 18 or newer and React DOM are peer dependencies. Import the stylesheet once
near the application root and wrap the app in `GlassSystemProvider`:

```tsx
import "open-glass-ui/styles.css";
import { GlassSystemProvider } from "open-glass-ui";

export function Root({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <GlassSystemProvider theme={{ appearance: "system", defaultAppearance: "dark" }}>
      {children}
    </GlassSystemProvider>
  );
}
```

`GlassSystemProvider` combines the runtime policy, the theme boundary and the
global toast queue. Every recipe, `Glass` and `useToast` must render below it.
Without the stylesheet the components render as unstyled native elements and
`Glass` has no material, so never omit the import.

## 2. Imports

```tsx
import "open-glass-ui/styles.css";
import { Button, Glass, GlassSystemProvider, useToast } from "open-glass-ui";
import { WebGLGlassSurface } from "open-glass-ui/webgl"; // owned media only
import { contrastRatio, createGlassTheme } from "open-glass-ui/core"; // server-safe, no React
```

- `open-glass-ui`: providers, `Glass`, hooks, all forty recipes, theme and
  material utilities, renderer utilities and public types. It is a client entry
  (`"use client"`).
- `open-glass-ui/styles.css`: the recipe and design stylesheet.
- `open-glass-ui/core`: pure geometry, material, theme and quality helpers. It
  never imports React and can run in server components and build tools.
- `open-glass-ui/webgl`: the opt-in WebGL2 renderer and surface.
- Never import `@open-glass-ui/*`. Those workspace packages are private,
  inlined into this package and do not exist on npm.

## 3. Callback conventions (read this before writing a screen)

There is no single "value / onValueChange" convention. Some recipes take a
custom change callback with a typed value. Others are thin wrappers over a
native input and use the native `onChange` event. Using the wrong one is a type
error.

| Recipe | Value props | Change callback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SegmentedControl, Tabs, RadioGroup | `value`, `defaultValue` (string union `T`) | `onValueChange(value: T)` |
| SearchField | `value`, `defaultValue` (string) | `onValueChange(value: string)` |
| NumberField | `value`, `defaultValue` (number) | `onValueChange(value: number)`, plus native `onChange(event)` |
| Slider | native `value`, `defaultValue` (number, string or string array) | native `onChange(event)` and `onInput(event)`. No `onValueChange`. Read `Number(event.currentTarget.value)` |
| TextField, Textarea | native `value`, `defaultValue` | native `onChange(event)`. No `onValueChange` |
| Select | native `value`, `defaultValue` (string) | native `onChange(event)`. No `onValueChange` |
| Checkbox | native `checked`, `defaultChecked` | native `onChange(event)`. No `onCheckedChange` |
| Switch | `checked`, `defaultChecked` | `onCheckedChange(checked: boolean)` and native `onChange(event)` |
| ToggleButton | `pressed`, `defaultPressed` | `onPressedChange(pressed: boolean)` |
| Menu, Popover, Dialog, Drawer, Toast | `open`, `defaultOpen` | `onOpenChange(open: boolean)` |
| Pagination | `page`, `count` | `onPageChange(page: number)` |
| Stepper | `current` | `onStepChange(index: number)` |

Rules that follow from the table:

- A controlled input (`value` or `checked`) needs its change callback, or React
  warns and the field is read-only.
- Components that wrap a native element forward its other native props, so
  `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `placeholder`,
  `autoComplete`, `onBlur` and `aria-*` all work. A generated `id`, `name`
  (defaults to the id) and label association are added for you.
- `Button` defaults to `type="button"`, so it never submits a form by accident.

## 4. Component reference (all forty recipes)

Each entry lists the props interface, the props you must pass (`Required`) and
the callbacks it declares (`Callbacks`). `Native` lists native events that are
forwarded rather than declared. Everything else is optional. Components that
extend an HTML element type also accept that element's native props and
`className`. `T` is the string union of the item values and is inferred from
the `items` you pass, so `onValueChange` receives a narrowed type.

### Button
Interface: `ButtonProps`
Required: none
Native: `onClick`, `onPointerMove`, `disabled`, `type`, `form`
Props: `variant` is `"primary" | "secondary" | "quiet" | "danger"` (default
`secondary`), `size` is `"small" | "medium" | "large"`, `leadingIcon` and
`trailingIcon` are nodes shown beside the label. Children are the label.

### IconButton
Interface: `IconButtonProps`
Required: `aria-label`, `children`
Native: `onClick`
Props: a `Button` that renders only the icon passed as children. Defaults to
`variant="quiet"`. The accessible name is mandatory.

### SegmentedControl
Interface: `SegmentedControlProps<T extends string>`
Required: `aria-label`, `items`
Callbacks: `onValueChange`
Props: `items: readonly { value: T; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }[]`,
`value?: T`, `defaultValue?: T` (defaults to the first item). Renders a
`fieldset` of toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`. Throws if there are no items
and no `defaultValue`.

### Switch
Interface: `SwitchProps`
Required: `label`
Callbacks: `onCheckedChange`
Native: `onChange`, `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `disabled`, `name`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `description?: ReactNode`, `labelProps?`. Renders an
input with `role="switch"`.

### Slider
Interface: `SliderProps`
Required: `label`
Native: `onChange`, `onInput`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `min`, `max`, `step`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `valueText?: string` (the visible and spoken value),
`unit?: string` (appended to the numeric value). `min` defaults to 0 and `max`
to 100. Renders a native range input and an `output`.

### Toolbar
Interface: `ToolbarProps`
Required: `label`
Props: `label: string` (the toolbar's accessible name), `orientation?:
"horizontal" | "vertical"`, `material?: "clear" | "regular" | "frosted"`,
`tone?: "light" | "dark" | "auto"`. Renders `role="toolbar"` on a `Glass`, so it
already paints a glass material.

### Dock
Interface: `DockProps`
Required: `label`
Props: `label: string` (names the `nav` landmark), `material?`, `tone?`. Renders
a `Glass` as a `nav`, so it already paints a glass material.

### Tabs
Interface: `TabsProps<T extends string>`
Required: `label`, `items`
Callbacks: `onValueChange`
Props: `label: string` (names the tablist),
`items: readonly { value: T; label: ReactNode; content: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }[]`,
`value?: T`, `defaultValue?: T` (defaults to the first enabled item). Each
item's `content` is the panel; only the active panel is rendered. Arrow, Home
and End keys move between tabs. Throws if no item is enabled.

### Menu
Interface: `MenuProps`
Required: `label`, `trigger`
Callbacks: `onOpenChange`
Props: `label: string` (becomes the trigger's accessible name and names the
menu), `trigger: ReactElement` (a single button element such as
`<Button>Actions</Button>`; the recipe adds the id, `aria-expanded` and click
handling), children are `MenuItem` elements. Optional: `material` (default
`frosted`), `tone`, `placement?: "start" | "center" | "end"`, `open`,
`defaultOpen`. The surface renders in a portal as a `Glass`.

### MenuItem
Interface: `MenuItemProps`
Required: none
Native: `onClick`, `disabled`
Props: `destructive?: boolean`. Use only inside a `Menu`. The menu closes after
`onClick` unless the handler calls `event.preventDefault()`.

### Popover
Interface: `PopoverProps`
Required: `label`, `trigger`
Callbacks: `onOpenChange`
Props: same shape as `Menu`, but the content is a free-form dialog. `label`
names the trigger and the popover. Children are any content.

### Tooltip
Interface: `TooltipProps`
Required: `label`, `children`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `children: ReactElement` (exactly one focusable
element; the tooltip adds `aria-describedby` to it), `placement?: "top" |
"bottom"`. A tooltip supplements a visible label; never put essential text only
in a tooltip.

### MediaControls
Interface: `MediaControlsProps`
Required: `playing`, `currentTime`, `duration`, `onPlayingChange`, `onSeek`
Callbacks: `onPlayingChange`, `onSeek`, `onMutedChange`
Props: `playing: boolean`, `currentTime: number`, `duration: number` (seconds),
`onPlayingChange(playing: boolean)`, `onSeek(time: number)`, `muted?: boolean`,
`onMutedChange?(muted: boolean)`. The mute button renders only when
`onMutedChange` is passed. The component is a controlled view; it does not
touch a media element, so you wire it to your `<video>` yourself.

### Badge
Interface: `BadgeProps`
Required: none
Props: `tone?: "neutral" | "accent" | "positive" | "warning" | "danger"`.
Children are the text.

### Avatar
Interface: `AvatarProps`
Required: `name`
Props: `name: string` (the accessible name; initials are derived from it),
`src?: string`, `size?: "small" | "medium" | "large"`.

### AvatarGroup
Interface: inline
Required: none
Props: a `div` that lays out `Avatar` children as an overlapping stack.

### Card
Interface: `CardProps`
Required: none
Native: `onClick`
Callbacks: `onPress`
Props: `eyebrow?: ReactNode`, `title?: ReactNode`, `footer?: ReactNode`,
`interactive?: boolean` (hover styling only, no focus), `onPress?: () => void`
(makes the card a keyboard-operable `role="button"`). Children are the body. A
card already paints its own surface; do not wrap it in `Glass`.

### Stat
Interface: `StatProps`
Required: `label`, `value`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `value: ReactNode`, `change?: ReactNode`, `tone?`
(same union as `Badge`).

### Progress
Interface: `ProgressProps`
Required: `label`, `value`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `value: number`, `max?: number` (default 100). Renders
a native `progress` with a percentage readout.

### Meter
Interface: `MeterProps`
Required: `label`, `value`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `value: number`, `min?`, `max?`, `low?`, `high?`,
`optimum?` (defaults 0, 100, 30, 75, 90). Renders a native `meter`.

### Spinner
Interface: inline
Required: none
Props: `label?: string` (default `"Loading"`, announced through `role="status"`).

### Skeleton
Interface: inline
Required: none
Props: `width?: string` (a CSS length, default `"100%"`). Decorative and hidden
from assistive technology.

### Alert
Interface: `AlertProps`
Required: `title`
Callbacks: `onDismiss`
Props: `title: ReactNode`, `tone?` (same union as `Badge`), `onDismiss?: () => void`
(shows a dismiss button). Children are the description. `tone="danger"` uses
`role="alert"`; other tones use `role="status"`.

### Banner
Interface: `BannerProps`
Required: `title`
Callbacks: `onDismiss`
Props: `title: ReactNode`, `action?: ReactNode`, `dismissible?: boolean`,
`onDismiss?: () => void`. Children are the message. A dismissed banner removes
itself.

### Breadcrumbs
Interface: inline
Required: `items`
Props: `items: readonly { label: string; href?: string }[]`. The last item is
the current page and is not a link.

### Pagination
Interface: `PaginationProps`
Required: `page`, `count`, `onPageChange`
Callbacks: `onPageChange`
Props: `page: number` (1-based), `count: number` (total pages),
`onPageChange(page: number)`. Pass an `aria-label` when a page has more than
one pagination.

### Accordion
Interface: inline
Required: `items`
Props: `items: readonly { id: string; title: ReactNode; content: ReactNode }[]`,
`multiple?: boolean`, `defaultOpenIds?: readonly string[]` (the first item is
open when omitted; pass `[]` to start collapsed), `headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`
(default 3). It manages its own open state.

### Dialog
Interface: `OverlayProps`
Required: `title`, `children`
Callbacks: `onOpenChange`
Props: `title: string`, `children: ReactNode` (the dialog body),
`description?: string`, `triggerLabel?: string` (renders a built-in trigger
button; omit it and drive the dialog with `open`/`onOpenChange`),
`open?: boolean`, `defaultOpen?: boolean`, `closeOnBackdrop?: boolean`
(default true). Renders in a portal, traps focus, closes on Escape, locks page
scroll, makes the rest of the page inert and returns focus to the opener.
`Dialog` and `Drawer` already paint a glass overlay surface.

### Drawer
Interface: `OverlayProps`
Required: `title`, `children`
Callbacks: `onOpenChange`
Props: identical to `Dialog`, rendered as a side sheet.

### Toast
Interface: `ToastProps`
Required: `title`
Callbacks: `onAction`, `onOpenChange`
Props: `title: ReactNode`, `actionLabel?: string`, `onAction?: () => void`,
`open?`, `defaultOpen?` (default true), `duration?: number` (milliseconds, 0
means persistent), `restoreLabel?: string`. This is the single-toast component.
For an app-wide queue use `useToast` (section 6) instead.

### Checkbox
Interface: `CheckboxProps`
Required: `label`
Native: `onChange`, `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `disabled`, `name`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `description?: ReactNode`.

### RadioGroup
Interface: `RadioGroupProps<T extends string>`
Required: `label`, `items`
Callbacks: `onValueChange`
Props: `label: string` (the group's accessible name),
`items: readonly { value: T; label: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }[]`,
`value?: T`, `defaultValue?: T`, `name?: string`, `disabled?: boolean`,
`className?: string`. It does not accept other native props.

### Select
Interface: `SelectProps`
Required: `label`, `options`
Native: `onChange`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `disabled`, `name`, `required`
Props: `label: ReactNode`,
`options: readonly { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }[]`.
Renders a native `select`. Read the choice from `event.currentTarget.value`.

### TextField
Interface: `TextFieldProps`
Required: `label`
Native: `onChange`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `type`, `name`, `required`, `placeholder`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `hint?: ReactNode`, `error?: ReactNode`. An `error`
sets `aria-invalid` and is announced; a `hint` is wired with `aria-describedby`.

### Textarea
Interface: `TextareaProps`
Required: `label`
Native: `onChange`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `rows`
Props: same as `TextField`, on a native `textarea`.

### SearchField
Interface: `SearchFieldProps`
Required: `label`
Callbacks: `onValueChange`
Props: `label: string` (visually hidden, used as the accessible name),
`value?: string`, `defaultValue?: string`, `onValueChange(value: string)`. A
clear button appears when there is text. The native `onChange` is not accepted.

### NumberField
Interface: `NumberFieldProps`
Required: `label`
Callbacks: `onValueChange`
Native: `onChange`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `disabled`
Props: `label: ReactNode`, `value?: number`, `defaultValue?: number` (default
0), `onValueChange(value: number)`, `decrementLabel?: string`,
`incrementLabel?: string`. Renders a native number input with stepper buttons.

### Stepper
Interface: inline
Required: `items`, `current`
Callbacks: `onStepChange`
Props: `items: readonly { id?: string; label: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode }[]`,
`current: number` (zero-based index of the active step),
`onStepChange?(index: number)`. Without `onStepChange` the steps are
non-interactive.

### ToggleButton
Interface: `ToggleButtonProps`
Required: none
Callbacks: `onPressedChange`
Native: `onClick`
Props: `pressed?: boolean`, `defaultPressed?: boolean`,
`onPressedChange?(pressed: boolean)`. Uses `aria-pressed`. Children are the label.

### FileDropzone
Interface: `FileDropzoneProps`
Required: `label`
Callbacks: `onFiles`, `onRejected`, `onInputChange`
Props: `label: string`, `name?: string`, `accept?: string` (an `accept` list
such as `"image/*,.pdf"`), `multiple?: boolean`, `maxSizeBytes?: number`,
`onFiles?(files: File[])`, `onRejected?(files: File[])` (files that fail
`accept` or `maxSizeBytes`), `onInputChange?(event)`. Wraps a real file input.

Exports: `useToast`, `ToastProvider`

Types you can import by name include `ButtonProps`, `TabsProps`, `TabItem`,
`SegmentItem`, `RadioItem`, `SelectOption`, `AccordionItem`, `BreadcrumbItem`,
`StepItem`, `OverlayProps`, `ToastOptions`, `ToastController`, `SemanticTone`,
`ButtonVariant` and `ControlSize`.

## 5. A complete screen

This example uses the exact prop shapes above and type-checks against the
package. `Menu` needs `trigger`, `Tabs` needs `items` with `content`, `Select`
needs `options`, and `Dialog` takes its body as children.

```tsx
import "open-glass-ui/styles.css";
import {
  Button,
  Card,
  Dialog,
  GlassSystemProvider,
  Menu,
  MenuItem,
  Select,
  Slider,
  Switch,
  Tabs,
  TextField,
  useToast,
} from "open-glass-ui";
import { useState } from "react";

function Settings() {
  const { toast } = useToast();
  const [volume, setVolume] = useState(40);
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState("system");
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Card eyebrow="Account" title="Preferences">
      <Tabs
        label="Settings sections"
        items={[
          {
            value: "general",
            label: "General",
            content: (
              <>
                <TextField
                  label="Display name"
                  value={name}
                  onChange={(event) => setName(event.currentTarget.value)}
                />
                <Select
                  label="Theme"
                  value={theme}
                  onChange={(event) => setTheme(event.currentTarget.value)}
                  options={[
                    { value: "system", label: "System" },
                    { value: "light", label: "Light" },
                    { value: "dark", label: "Dark" },
                  ]}
                />
                <Slider
                  label="Volume"
                  unit="%"
                  value={volume}
                  onChange={(event) => setVolume(Number(event.currentTarget.value))}
                />
                <Switch
                  label="Email updates"
                  defaultChecked
                  onCheckedChange={(checked) => console.log(checked)}
                />
              </>
            ),
          },
          { value: "danger", label: "Danger zone", content: <p>Be careful here.</p> },
        ]}
      />

      <Menu label="More actions" trigger={<Button variant="quiet">More</Button>}>
        <MenuItem onClick={() => toast({ title: "Saved", description: "Preferences updated." })}>
          Save
        </MenuItem>
        <MenuItem destructive onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
          Delete account
        </MenuItem>
      </Menu>

      <Dialog
        title="Delete account?"
        description="This cannot be undone."
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
      >
        <Button variant="danger" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
          Delete
        </Button>
      </Dialog>
    </Card>
  );
}

export function App() {
  return (
    <GlassSystemProvider>
      <Settings />
    </GlassSystemProvider>
  );
}
```

## 6. Toasts

`GlassSystemProvider` includes the toast queue and renders its viewport in a
portal. Call `useToast` in any component below it:

```tsx
import { Button, useToast } from "open-glass-ui";

export function SaveButton() {
  const { toast } = useToast();
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
        toast({
          title: "Theme saved",
          description: "Neutral contrast settings are now active.",
          actionLabel: "Undo",
          onAction: () => console.log("undo"),
          duration: 6000, // ms; 0 keeps it until dismissed
        })
      }
    >
      Save theme
    </Button>
  );
}
```

- `useToast()` returns `{ toast, dismiss }`. `toast(options)` returns the new
  toast's id; `dismiss(id)` closes it.
- `ToastOptions` is `{ title: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode;
  actionLabel?: string; onAction?: () => void; duration?: number }`.
- It throws "useToast must be used within a ToastProvider." outside a provider.
  If you build providers yourself, render `ToastProvider` inside
  `GlassThemeProvider` and `GlassProvider`, or pass `toasts={false}` to
  `GlassSystemProvider` and supply your own.
- `GlassSystemProvider toasts={{ defaultDuration, maxVisible, label }}`
  configures the queue (defaults 5000 ms, 3 visible, "Notifications").
- Timed toasts pause while hovered or focused and close on Escape.

## 7. Providers, themes and design

`GlassSystemProvider` props: `children`, `renderer`, `quality`, `motion`,
`theme`, `toasts`, `design`.

- `renderer`: `"auto"` (default, CSS-first), `"css"`, `"organic-svg"`,
  `"sdf-svg"` or `"webgl2"`. Unsupported choices fall back to CSS.
- `quality`: `"auto"`, `"low"`, `"medium"` or `"high"`.
- `motion`: `"system"` (follow `prefers-reduced-motion`), `"on"` or `"off"`.
- `design`: `"liquid"` (default since 0.4) or `"classic"` (the 0.3 look).
- `theme`: the `GlassThemeProvider` props below, as one object.
- `toasts`: queue options, or `false` to opt out.

`GlassThemeProvider` props (also the shape of `GlassSystemProvider`'s `theme`):

- `appearance`: `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"` (default `"system"`).
- `defaultAppearance`: `"light"` or `"dark"`. What the server and the first
  client render use before `system` resolves. Default `"dark"`.
- `theme`: `{ preset, accent, secondary, tertiary, contrast, radius, glass }`.
  `preset` is `neutral`, `cobalt`, `teal`, `violet`, `coral` or `amber`.
  `accent`, `secondary` and `tertiary` are 3- or 6-digit hex (invalid values
  throw). `contrast` is `standard` or `high` (default `high`). `radius` is
  `sharp`, `balanced` or `soft` (default `soft` in liquid, `balanced` in
  classic). `glass` is a look (section 11).
- `design`: `"liquid"` or `"classic"`. Scopes nest and the nearest one wins:

```tsx
<GlassSystemProvider design="classic">
  <LegacyArea />
  <GlassThemeProvider design="liquid">
    <NewArea />
  </GlassThemeProvider>
</GlassSystemProvider>
```

- `className`, `style` and other `div` props go on the `.ogui-theme` wrapper
  element the provider renders.

Lower-level pieces: `GlassProvider` (runtime policy only), `GlassThemeProvider`
(theme only) and `ToastProvider` can be used separately.

Hooks: `useGlassRuntime()` returns `{ capabilities, renderer, quality, motion,
hydrated }`; `useGlassCapabilities()` returns the capability probe;
`useGlassTheme()` returns `{ appearance, preference, palette, tokens, hydrated,
design }`.

Exports: `GlassSystemProvider`, `GlassProvider`, `GlassThemeProvider`, `Glass`,
`GlassGroup`, `GlassSource`, `SdfFilterDefinition`, `OrganicFilterDefinition`,
`useGlassCapabilities`, `useGlassRuntime`, `useGlassTheme`, `useGlassGroup`,
`useGlassPointerField`, `useSdfFilter`, `createGlassTheme`,
`createGlassThemeTokens`, `contrastRatio`, `relativeLuminance`,
`readableForeground`, `getMaterialPreset`, `GLASS_LOOK_PRESETS`

## 8. Tokens and scoping

The theme provider writes semantic `--ogui-*` custom properties inline on its
`.ogui-theme` element:

```text
--ogui-color-background  --ogui-color-canvas
--ogui-color-surface     --ogui-color-surface-strong
--ogui-color-text        --ogui-color-muted
--ogui-color-border      --ogui-color-border-strong
--ogui-color-control     --ogui-color-control-hover   --ogui-color-control-active
--ogui-color-accent      --ogui-color-accent-ink      --ogui-color-accent-soft
--ogui-color-accent-highlight-mix
--ogui-color-secondary   --ogui-color-tertiary        --ogui-color-focus
--ogui-color-danger      --ogui-color-danger-ink
--ogui-color-success     --ogui-color-success-ink
--ogui-color-warning     --ogui-color-warning-ink
--ogui-radius-control    --ogui-radius-surface        --ogui-radius-capsule
```

Where to override them:

- Because the provider writes the tokens inline on its own element, a
  `:root { --ogui-color-accent: ... }` rule has no effect: the inline value on a
  closer element always wins. Do not override tokens on `:root`, `html` or
  `body`.
- Preferred: the typed `theme` input (`theme={{ theme: { preset, accent } }}`).
- Or pass the token through the provider's `style` (or `className`), for
  example `theme={{ style: { "--ogui-color-accent": "#185fd1" } as CSSProperties }}`
  (the cast is needed because TypeScript's style type omits custom properties).
- Or set it on a descendant class, which affects everything inside it:

```css
.billing-zone {
  --ogui-color-accent: #22705c;
  --ogui-color-accent-ink: #ffffff;
  --ogui-color-focus: #22705c;
  /* Light ink on a mid-tone accent: lower the highlight, for example 0% to
     8%, so the label keeps its contrast. */
  --ogui-color-accent-highlight-mix: 8%;
}
```

When you override `--ogui-color-accent` locally, also set
`--ogui-color-accent-ink` and the focus colour, and for a light ink on a
mid-tone accent lower `--ogui-color-accent-highlight-mix`. Then check contrast.

`--ogui-color-accent-highlight-mix` is a percentage (default `16%`): how much
white the liquid primary button mixes into its top highlight. The theme lowers
it automatically when needed so the accent ink keeps 4.5:1 contrast. Accent ink
is chosen so text on liquid accent fills keeps at least 4.5:1 against the
rendered fill; that guarantee applies to the default liquid design, while
classic keeps its 0.3 rendering and only receives the corrected ink.

Which tokens recipes actually read:

- `--ogui-color-surface`, `-surface-strong`, `-border-strong`, `-secondary`,
  `-tertiary`, `-accent-soft` and `-background` are for your own CSS. No recipe
  reads them.
- In the classic design, controls read `--ogui-color-control`, `-hover`,
  `-active` for fills, `--ogui-color-border` for hairlines and
  `--ogui-radius-control` for corners.
- In the liquid design those three groups do not apply to controls. Liquid reads
  its own public control tokens instead:

```text
--ogui-lg-fill          control fill (rest)
--ogui-lg-fill-hover    control fill on hover
--ogui-lg-fill-active   control fill while pressed
--ogui-lg-hairline      control and field hairline
--ogui-radius-capsule   corner radius of capsule controls (buttons, toggles,
                        segments, tabs); 999px by default, 0.5rem with
                        radius "sharp"
--ogui-radius-surface   corner radius of cards, overlays and panels
```

  In liquid, setting `--ogui-radius-control` does not change buttons; use
  `--ogui-radius-capsule`. Setting `--ogui-color-control` or
  `--ogui-color-border` does not recolour liquid controls; use the `--ogui-lg-*`
  tokens. `--ogui-color-text`, `-muted`, `-accent`, `-accent-ink`, `-focus`,
  `-danger` and `-success` still apply in both designs.
- Liquid re-resolves its fills on every liquid scope root and on every `Glass`
  element, and each of those overrides the value it inherits. Set
  `--ogui-lg-fill*` on the provider (`className` or `style`) for controls outside
  any `Glass`, and on the `Glass` (`className`) for controls inside it. One
  selector covers a region: `.scope, .scope [data-ogui-glass] { --ogui-lg-fill:
  ...; }`. A rule on a plain wrapper `div` does not reach controls inside a
  `Glass`.
- The overall glass look is set with the `--ogui-glass-*` multipliers
  (section 11), which are public and work from plain CSS on any theme boundary
  or `Glass`.
- `--ogui-material-*` (background, border, highlight, shadow, text, muted, filter,
  dim) are written by each `Glass`. They are an advanced surface; prefer the
  theme tokens.

Public theme helpers (also from `open-glass-ui/core`): `createGlassTheme`,
`createGlassThemeTokens`, `contrastRatio`, `relativeLuminance`,
`readableForeground`. `createGlassTheme` derives a readable accent foreground;
still verify contrast in the real layout.

## 9. Tailwind CSS v4 and cascade layers

Unlayered CSS beats layered CSS regardless of specificity. The library
stylesheet is unlayered, so with Tailwind v4 (whose utilities live in
`@layer utilities`) a utility such as `rounded-lg` or `bg-red-500` on an
OpenGlass component loses to the recipe styles. Fix it by importing the library
into its own layer, ordered between Tailwind's `base` and `components`. Put this
at the top of your main CSS file, before `@import "tailwindcss"`:

```css
@layer theme, base, ogui, components, utilities;
@import "open-glass-ui/styles.css" layer(ogui);
@import "tailwindcss";
```

Do not also import `open-glass-ui/styles.css` in JavaScript, or the unlayered
copy comes back. With this order, utilities override recipe styles, recipe
styles override Tailwind's preflight, and your own unlayered CSS overrides both.

`Glass` (and the recipes drawn through it: Toolbar, Dock, Menu and Popover
surfaces) writes its material inline, so utilities still restyle its shape and
spacing but not its background, border color, shadow or backdrop filter. Change
the material with the `look` prop, the `--ogui-glass-*` tokens, or the `style`
prop.

The same layering works with any other layered CSS setup.

## 10. Typography

Recipes use `font: inherit`; the library ships no font family. A bare page
renders in the browser default serif. Set a font on the application:

```css
body {
  font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

With Tailwind, set it in your theme or on `body`. The provider wrapper does not
set a font.

## 11. Glass, already-glass recipes and tone over imagery

`Glass` is the low-level material surface. Props: `as` (`div`, `section`,
`nav`, `aside`, `span`), `material` (`"clear"`, `"regular"`, `"frosted"`),
`tone` (`"light"`, `"dark"` or `"auto"`), `renderer`, `source`, `interactive`,
`optics`, `geometry`, `filterId`, `look`, plus native element props.

Already glass: `Toolbar`, `Dock`, `Menu` and `Popover` render a `Glass`;
`Dialog`, `Drawer` and `Toast` paint a glass overlay surface; `Card` paints its
own translucent surface. Do not wrap any of them in `<Glass>`: it double-wraps
the material. Use `<Glass>` for custom regions (a hero panel, a sidebar, a
floating bar) and put plain recipes such as `Button`, `Switch` and `Slider`
inside it. Use glass selectively for controls, navigation and transient
surfaces, not for content-dense cards and tables.

Material look (liquid design). `theme={{ theme: { glass } }}` or
`<Glass look={...}>` takes a preset (`liquid`, `frosted`, `clear`, `smoked`,
`lensed`) or multipliers `{ blur, opacity, tint, saturation, brightness, rim,
highlight, lightAngle, lightSpread, lensing, shadow }` (1 is the default;
`lightAngle` is degrees with 0 at the top; `tint` may be `{ dark, light }`).
They map to `--ogui-glass-*` variables.

Placing glass over photos or video: force the tone of the surface so its
material and text match the image, whatever the app theme is.

```tsx
<Glass tone="dark" material="frosted" style={{ padding: 16, borderRadius: 24 }}>
  <p>Caption over a photo</p>
  <Button>Share</Button>
</Glass>
```

In releases after 0.4.0, a `Glass` whose `tone` differs from the surrounding
appearance also switches its text, muted text, borders and control tokens to
that tone, and nested recipes and nested `Glass` follow it. In 0.4.0 only the
material changes, so text inside inherits the app theme colours. Keep a
legible background behind it and check contrast over the real image.
`Menu`, `Popover` and `Toolbar` accept the same `tone` prop.

`optics` and the renderer: `optics` accepts a partial material
(`thickness`, `ior`, `dispersion`, `edgeStrength`, `bevel`, `frost`). Only
`frost` changes the glass material on every renderer path. The other fields do
not change `Glass` pixels, and switching `renderer` does not make them apply.
Refraction comes from two other inputs, which take their own material object:
`useSdfFilter({ material })` and a WebGL lens's `material`. Share one object
between them when you want a consistent look (see section 12).

## 12. Renderers: CSS, SDF/SVG and WebGL2

- `renderer="auto"` is CSS-first. It never silently escalates to SVG or WebGL.
  The CSS material uses blur, tint, border and shadow; it implies refraction but
  does not bend page pixels.
- SDF/SVG refraction is explicit, for stable geometry. WebGL2 is explicit, for an
  image, canvas or video you own. Both fall back to CSS when unsupported.
- Forced colors and reduced transparency always select the accessible CSS path.

Use cases:

```text
arbitrary DOM                              -> Glass with the default CSS material
stable DOM shape needing refraction        -> useSdfFilter + SdfFilterDefinition
owned image/canvas/video needing refraction-> open-glass-ui/webgl
```

### SDF/SVG: a decorative filtered layer

`filterId` applies an SVG `filter: url(#id)` to the `Glass` element. A filter
displaces everything that element paints, including its children, so putting
text or controls inside a filtered `Glass` distorts them and breaks legibility
and selection. Filter a decorative layer instead, and keep the real content in
an unfiltered sibling above it:

```tsx
import {
  Glass,
  getMaterialPreset,
  SdfFilterDefinition,
  useSdfFilter,
} from "open-glass-ui";

const geometry = {
  kind: "rounded-rect",
  width: 320,
  height: 160,
  cornerRadius: 28,
} as const;
const material = { ...getMaterialPreset("regular"), thickness: 0.8 };

export function RefractedPanel({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const filter = useSdfFilter({
    id: "panel",
    width: 320,
    height: 160,
    geometry,
    material,
    quality: "medium",
  });

  return (
    <div style={{ position: "relative", width: 320, height: 160 }}>
      <SdfFilterDefinition filter={filter} />
      <Glass
        aria-hidden="true"
        renderer="sdf-svg"
        filterId={filter.filterId}
        geometry={geometry}
        style={{ position: "absolute", inset: 0 }}
      />
      <div style={{ position: "relative" }}>{children}</div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Supported shapes: `circle`, `capsule`, `rounded-rect`, `superellipse`.
Pass `quality` (`"low"`, `"medium"` or `"high"`) explicitly. Regenerate the map
only when size, geometry, material or quality changes, not when the element
moves. The map is
encoded after mount, so server and hydration output stays the CSS baseline.
`OrganicFilterDefinition` plus `renderer="organic-svg"` is an expressive,
decorative option; keep it away from text and respect reduced motion.

### WebGL2: owned media only

`WebGLGlassSurface` samples an HTML image, canvas or video (or an
`ImageBitmap`, `ImageData` or `OffscreenCanvas`) that you own, through
`sourceRef`. It cannot sample arbitrary page pixels. At most six lenses share one
source. Keep text and controls in the DOM, never in the canvas.

The surface only needs the runtime policy (capabilities and quality), and a
canvas over media has no themed DOM, which is why this example uses
`GlassProvider`. Use `GlassSystemProvider` instead if the same tree also renders
recipes.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef } from "react";
import { GlassProvider, getMaterialPreset } from "open-glass-ui";
import { WebGLGlassSurface } from "open-glass-ui/webgl";

// One material object drives both refraction paths.
const material = getMaterialPreset("clear");

export function MediaLens() {
  const sourceRef = useRef<HTMLVideoElement>(null);

  return (
    <GlassProvider>
      <video ref={sourceRef} src="/demo.mp4" muted playsInline autoPlay loop />
      <WebGLGlassSurface
        sourceRef={sourceRef}
        continuous
        maxDevicePixelRatio={2}
        lenses={[{ x: 240, y: 140, width: 220, height: 92, radius: 0.36, material }]}
      />
    </GlassProvider>
  );
}
```

The same `material` can be passed to `useSdfFilter({ ..., material })` for a
matching SDF layer elsewhere. Props: `sourceRef`, `lenses`, `continuous`
(only for animated sources), `renderKey`, `maxDevicePixelRatio` (default 2),
`onStatusChange`, `onRendererError`, plus canvas attributes. Keep the original
media and its fallback in the DOM.

## 13. Accessibility modes, SSR and Next.js

The target is WCAG 2.2 AA, not certification. Semantics, focus and interaction
stay in native DOM. Reduced motion, reduced transparency and forced colors are
designed states: motion stops, glass becomes opaque with equivalent hierarchy,
and forced colors hands rendering to the system palette. Give every control a
visible label or accessible name, and test over real backgrounds.

The server renders semantic content with the CSS baseline; the client provider
probes capabilities and preferences after hydration. Do not read `window`,
`document`, `matchMedia`, canvas or WebGL during render, and do not branch
initial markup on capability. In the Next.js App Router, put providers and any
component that uses hooks or recipes behind `"use client"`:

```tsx
"use client";

import "open-glass-ui/styles.css";
import { GlassSystemProvider } from "open-glass-ui";

export function OpenGlassRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <GlassSystemProvider>{children}</GlassSystemProvider>;
}
```

Pure helpers from `open-glass-ui/core` may run in server components.

## 14. Common mistakes

1. Using `onValueChange` on Slider, TextField, Textarea, Select, Checkbox or
   Switch. Use native `onChange` (and `onCheckedChange` on Switch). See section 3.
2. Omitting `trigger` on `Menu` or `Popover`, `items` on `Tabs`, or `options` on
   `Select`. They are required and have fixed shapes (section 4).
3. Giving `IconButton`, `SegmentedControl`, `Toolbar`, `Dock`, `Tabs`, `Menu`,
   `Popover`, `RadioGroup` or `SearchField` no accessible label.
4. Wrapping `Card`, `Toolbar`, `Dock`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `Menu` or `Popover` in
   `<Glass>`. They already paint a material.
5. Calling `useToast` outside `GlassSystemProvider`, or forgetting the braces:
   `const { toast } = useToast();`.
6. Overriding `--ogui-*` tokens on `:root`. The provider writes them inline;
   use the `theme` prop, the provider `style`, or a descendant class.
7. Setting `--ogui-radius-control` or `--ogui-color-control` and expecting liquid
   buttons to change. Use `--ogui-radius-capsule` and `--ogui-lg-fill*`.
8. Importing the stylesheet unlayered next to Tailwind v4 and then fighting
   utilities. Use the layer setup in section 9.
9. Leaving the page without a font. Recipes inherit it.
10. Applying `filterId` to a `Glass` that contains text or controls. Filter a
    decorative sibling layer instead.
11. Expecting `optics` thickness, ior or dispersion to change `Glass`, or a
    different `renderer` to enable them. Only `frost` applies; refraction uses
    `useSdfFilter({ material })` or a WebGL lens material.
12. Using `renderer="webgl2"` on arbitrary DOM. WebGL needs an owned media source.
13. Importing `@open-glass-ui/*` or deep paths. Use the three public entries.
14. Rendering the provider or hook-using components in a Next.js server
    component. Add `"use client"`.

## Checklist before returning generated code

1. Import the stylesheet once and render everything below `GlassSystemProvider`.
2. Use an existing recipe before building a custom control.
3. Match each recipe's required props and callback names from section 4.
4. Default to the CSS renderer and semantic DOM.
5. Add labels, keep keyboard behavior, and keep Next.js output hydration-stable.
6. Type-check against the installed package, and test keyboard, focus, reduced
   motion, forced colors, contrast and mobile overflow.

More detail: https://github.com/moekoelueker/open-glass-ui/tree/main/docs
